title: MCP delete_record refuses a call without confirm: true (ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED), the run_action confirmation gate widened to deletes
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ② maintainer-directed task. Maintainer, verbatim (Claude Code session, 2026-11-06): 「同意」, then, after an isolated contract-review-tier re-read flagged that this is a breaking change for every MCP client that deletes and recommended deferring a `data:delete` scope split, again 「同意」. Option B of the seat's analysis. Routing, verbatim: 「能交给车队开发的你不要自己开发」.

Clause-②: yes (the confirmation contract in `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` widens to a second door; the error-code ledger gains a producer site).

## Problem (customer-visible)

An AI agent connected over MCP can hard-delete a record with one call. `delete_record` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:1481-1499`) carries only `annotations.destructiveHint: true`, a hint the client may ignore. Its server path (`bridge.remove`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts:1146-1166`) enforces API exposure (`apiOperations` may exclude `delete` → 405) and credentials, but has no confirmation step. Deletes are hard (`enable.trash` retired, soft delete parked: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:82-83,168-175`). An instruction injected into a record's text can therefore lead an agent to delete records the user may delete, with no human asked.

## Decision context

`run_action` already refuses an author-gated action without `confirm: true` (`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`; #15942, PR #17486 +834/−15; contract #16293 / PR #16531). The runtime's own note (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:2848-2860`): the gate "makes forgetting loud. It does not prove a human", REST is outside, and "widening the set is its own decision, not a thing to infer". This card is that decision, for `delete_record` only.

## Ask

1. `delete_record` refuses a call without `confirm: true` with `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, reusing `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_MEMBER` (closed boolean, `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts:240`) and the same refusal shape and `details` as `run_action`. The tool description tells the agent to ask the human first, then retry. Nothing is deleted on a refused call.
2. **Scope:** the MCP `delete_record` tool only. REST `DELETE /api/v1/data/...` (the human path) stays outside, as in #17486's changeset. `update_record` is not gated. No per-object exemption for now. Any future bulk-delete tool must take the same gate. State all four in the changeset.
3. **Breaking change:** every MCP client that deletes is refused until it sends `confirm`. Ship a `minor` changeset with a FROM → TO block (precedent `.changeset/action-confirmation-gate-enforced.md`).
4. Update the contract docblock in `ai-service.ts` to name the second door, and the error-code ledger's provenance for the new producer site.
5. **Tests:** refused without `confirm`, record intact; deleted with `confirm: true`; the refusal's code and details; REST delete unaffected.

Considered and not built now: an OAuth `data:delete` scope split (today `data:write` bundles create, update and delete, `mcp-http-tools.ts:220`; a real authorization lever, deferred for want of pull: a permanent new scope value); a record-bound confirmation token (adds nothing while `confirm` is an attestation); MCP elicitation (no support in `packages/mcp` today). Elicitation or client-side approval is the mainstream end state; this gate stays as the server-side backstop. Cloud's service-ai chat exposes no raw delete tool at all, so nothing to change there.

Size: S–M (mcp tool, tests, changeset, contract docblock); precedent #17486 +834/−15, which also carried the runtime gate.

Reader: the `domain:server` lane seat, from `pm:queue`.
